text:
Cornell University, founded in 1865 by Ezra Cornell and Andrew Dickson White, is New York State's land-grant institution with a main campus in Ithaca. Known for its technological innovation and academic excellence, Cornell has developed 16 colleges (including privately endowed and publicly supported statutory colleges) and expanded internationally through programs like Weill Cornell Medicine in Qatar and Cornell Tech in New York City. The university operates on a 4–1–4 academic calendar and offers highly competitive undergraduate and graduate programs, with a current endowment of $10.7 billion and world-class research facilities in science, engineering, humanities, and conservation—including the Cornell Botanic Gardens and numerous specialized labs.
Cornell consistently ranks among the top academic institutions globally, with prominent contributions in fields like architecture, business, and international relations. It supports an active student life with more than 1,000 organizations, a robust Greek scene, and NCAA Division I athletics. Notable alumni include heads of state, Nobel laureates, inventors, authors, and public figures. Cornell's decentralized governance includes a diverse Board of Trustees and relies heavily on philanthropic support for academic development. As of October 2024, Cornell counts more than 250,000 living alumni and 62 affiliated Nobel laureates, sustaining its legacy as a leading research university both nationally and worldwide.
